_note: Public-domain historical/biographical chronology of the contributors whose Bani is recorded in Sri Guru Granth Sahib Ji. Dates are widely-cited approximations (scholarly ranges vary, especially for the Bhagats and Bhatts); 'circa' flags the most uncertain. 'name' matches the corpus author string exactly so the UI can join live Ang/line data. This is historical context only — never a ranking.

contributors.name: Sheikh Farid Ji
contributors.blurb: Revered Sufi saint of Punjab; his saloks and shabads are the earliest Bani in the Granth.

contributors.name: Bhagat Jaidev Ji
contributors.blurb: Sanskrit-influenced devotional poet, author of the Gita Govinda tradition.

contributors.name: Bhagat Trilochan Ji
contributors.blurb: Maharashtrian sant, a contemporary and associate of Namdev.

contributors.name: Bhagat Namdev Ji
contributors.blurb: Beloved Marathi sant of pure devotion; the most-represented Bhagat after Kabir.

contributors.name: Bhagat Ramanand Ji
contributors.blurb: Influential Bhakti teacher of the Ganges plain, traditionally linked to Kabir and Ravidas.

contributors.name: Bhagat Kabir Ji
contributors.blurb: The towering weaver-mystic; his verses on the formless One are the most extensive Bhagat Bani.

contributors.name: Bhagat Ravidas Ji
contributors.blurb: Cobbler-saint of radical equality, a contemporary of Kabir.

contributors.name: Bhagat Beni Ji
contributors.blurb: A sant of yogic and devotional verse; biographical detail is scarce.

contributors.name: Bhagat Bhikhan Ji
contributors.blurb: A sant whose two shabads sit among the Bhagat Bani.

contributors.name: Bhai Mardana
contributors.blurb: Guru Nanak's lifelong rabābī and companion on the udasis; a few saloks are his.

contributors.name: Guru Nanak Dev Ji (M1)
contributors.blurb: The first Guru and founder; the Mool Mantar and Japji open the Granth with his revelation.

contributors.name: Guru Angad Dev Ji (M2)
contributors.blurb: Second Guru; shaped the Gurmukhi script and contributed saloks within the Vaars.

contributors.name: Guru Amar Das Ji (M3)
contributors.blurb: Third Guru; author of the Anand Sahib and a vast body of Bani across many raags.

contributors.name: Guru Ram Das Ji (M4)
contributors.blurb: Fourth Guru, founder of Amritsar; his Lavan are the wedding hymns of Sikh marriage.

contributors.name: Guru Arjan Dev Ji (M5)
contributors.blurb: Fifth Guru and compiler of the Adi Granth (1604); the most-represented voice, author of Sukhmani Sahib.

contributors.name: Baba Sundar Ji
contributors.blurb: Author of the Sadu, the composition on a peaceful, God-willed passing.

contributors.name: Satta & Balwand
contributors.blurb: The two rabābīs whose Vaar praises the light passing from Guru to Guru.

contributors.name: Bhatt Kalsahar (ਭਟ)
contributors.blurb: The most prolific of the Bhatts, the court bards who praised the Gurus in Savaiye.

contributors.name: Bhatt Nal (ਭਟ)
contributors.blurb: One of the eleven Bhatts whose Savaiye honour the Gurus.

contributors.name: Bhatt Mathura (ਭਟ)
contributors.blurb: A Bhatt whose verses especially praise Guru Ram Das and Guru Arjan.

contributors.name: The Bhatts (ਭਟ)
contributors.blurb: The collective body of the Bhatt bards whose Savaiye sit near the close of the Granth.

contributors.name: Bhatt Kirat (ਭਟ)
contributors.blurb: One of the eleven Bhatts of the Guru's court.

contributors.name: Bhatt Gayand (ਭਟ)
contributors.blurb: A Bhatt celebrated for the rhythmic force of his Savaiye.

contributors.name: Bhatt Jalap (ਭਟ)
contributors.blurb: One of the eleven Bhatts whose praise is recorded in the Granth.

contributors.name: Bhatt Sal (ਭਟ)
contributors.blurb: A Bhatt of the Guru's court.

contributors.name: Bhatt Bhikha (ਭਟ)
contributors.blurb: One of the eleven Bhatts whose Savaiye honour the Gurus.

contributors.name: Bhatt Bal (ਭਟ)
contributors.blurb: A Bhatt of the Guru's court.

contributors.name: Bhatt Haribans (ਭਟ)
contributors.blurb: One of the eleven Bhatts; his is among the closing Savaiye.

contributors.name: Bhatt Bhal (ਭਟ)
contributors.blurb: A Bhatt of the Guru's court.

contributors.name: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji (M9)
contributors.blurb: Ninth Guru; his saloks of detachment and courage were added by Guru Gobind Singh.
